Author: Rahul Bharti

 At Jammu

Chandeer Shekhar Bali ....Appellant(s)
 Through :- Mr. Divyanshu Malhotra, Advocate.
 V/s
New India Assurance Co. ltd and ors. ....Respondent(s)
 Through :- Mr. Udhay Bhasker, Advocate.

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge
 Order

19.08.2023 Mr. Divyanshu Malhotra, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant came to be acquitted of the charge of commission of offence under sections 338, 279, 337 RPC registered under FIR no. 156/2010 by the Court of Judicial Magistrate (Additional), Samba vide judgment dated 29.08.2016 as such this development has an effect with respect to the impugned award dated 28.06.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jammu on claim petition no. 188/2011 which was preferred by the appellant seeking compensation for the injuries received by him in the accident in which he came to be booked for his alleged act of rash and negligent driving resulting in registration of FIR no. 156/2010 and presentation of a challan against him before the Court of Judicial Magistrate (Additional), Samba and eventually resulting in his acquittal.

Mr. Malhotra, learned counsel for the appellant submits that in view of this development, the matter needs to be remanded back for de novo adjudication by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Jammu.

sentences.text:
The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jammu has dismissed the claim petition filed by the appellant by returning a finding on issues no. 1 and 4 which issues read as under:
(i) Whether an accident took place on 26.10.2010 near Bari Brahmana NHW by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. JK14-3130 by its driver respondent no. 3 as a result of which petitioner Chander Shekhar Bali received grievous injuries?
(ii) Whether the accident was due to negligence of the petitioner?

The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jammu came to hold that since there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the aforesaid vehicle bearing registration no. JK14-3130 and that it was the appellant whose negligence was in play as such the appellant was held not to be entitled for any compensation.
Mr. Malhotra, learned counsel for the appellant submits that since the appellant has come to be absolved of the charge of criminal negligence by the criminal court, the finding of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jammu needs to suffer revision on the basis of the evidence led by him.
Mr. Udhay Bhaskar Gupta, learned counsel appearing for the respondents needs to respond to the aforesaid state of submissions of Mr. Malhotra, learned counsel for the petitioner.
List again on 29.09.2023.
(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE JAMMU 19.08.2023 NARESH/Secy.
